chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abi Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of our companions, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The border of the Mosque of Sahlah is Rawha Rawha.

key_terms.الرَّوْحَاءُ: Rawha, a place name indicating the boundary
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ السَّهْلَةِ: Mosque of Sahlah, a prominent mosque in Kufah

ai.seo_question: What are the boundaries of the Mosque of Sahlah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the specific geographical boundaries (hadd) of the Mosque of Sahlah, extending its sanctity to the Rawha, a site historically significant for the burial of Imam Ali’s (AS) head before its final interment. By defining this limit, the narration underscores the ritual validity of prayers performed within this extended area, linking the physical space to the spiritual legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Mat Al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abī Muḥammad (Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faďďāl), from ‘Ali ibn Asbāť, from some of our companions, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

The border of the Mosque of Sahlah reaches Rawḥā. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn Walīd, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Ali ibn Asbāť, from some of our companions, from Imam Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
